name: Quinn Pereira
life: “I trained in a shop that made new hires pay for their name badges.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Quinn by a small Saturday habit. Quinn likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I practiced my handshake with the unaltered arm. The interviewer noticed and asked about the tailor.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. Quinn has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Quinn looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Quinn uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Quinn well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To keep the interview appointment with a jacket that feels like their own.
family: Cassandra Knight is Quinn’s older cousin. Quinn brings a spare shopping bag. Cassandra chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Cassandra says, “I was hired to value the gift. I asked whether the young woman wanted to be a landlord at all.”
connections: Norman Armas. The interviewer and applicant eventually discuss the deliberate switch of handshake. Also in the story is Alvin Chapman (hiring manager).
